answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging a burnable toll for every new identity: to open an account, an agent must destroy a small stake, the way a lotus sheds a petal each time it blooms. Honest participants pay once and begin their voyage, while attackers who wander across thousands of fake identities must pay for each one, so the cost of a sybil army grows linearly while its rewards stay capped by the same burn pool.
